Celle is a historic town in Lower Saxony, Germany, renowned for its medieval timber-framed houses—particularly in the Altstadt (Old Town)—and the ducal Celle Castle. Situated on the River Aller, it features a 17th-century theater, a 24-hour art museum, and a rich history as a former ducal residence. Celle Castle Key Highlights of Celle: Architecture: Known for having one of the highest concentrations of half-timbered houses in Germany, with over 400 restored timber-framed homes. The Hoppener Haus is a notable, ornate example. Celle Castle (Schloss Celle): A blend of Renaissance and Baroque architecture, featuring one of the oldest theaters in Germany and a chapel. Celle Castle Culture & Museums: Key attractions include the Bomann Museum (local history), Kunstmuseum Celle (modern art), and the historic Old Town. Bomann Museum Kunstmuseum Celle Location: Located near Hannover in Lower Saxony, it serves as a gateway to the southern Lüneburg Heath. Industry: Known for high-quality stem cell processing and research.
